strings.name: Neymar
strings.summary: Neymar emerged at Santos through dribbling, creativity and finishing. At Barcelona he formed an attacking partnership with Messi and Suárez and won European and Spanish titles. His 2017 Paris Saint-Germain transfer set a fee record; injuries later curtailed his Saudi spell. He returned to Santos in 2025, renewing through 2026, and retired from Brazil duty after the 2026 World Cup, having won Olympic gold in 2016.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A central Brazilian international and European club player with influence across continents in football culture.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Mogi das Cruzes, São Paulo state, Brazil.
strings.highlights.h1.title: European club treble
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won La Liga, Copa del Rey and Champions League with Barcelona in 2014–15.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Played futsal and street football, entering Santos's youth system in 2003.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Brazil's first men's Olympic gold
strings.highlights.h2.text: Scored the winning penalty in the 2016 final shootout.
strings.timeline.t1.title: International retirement
strings.timeline.t1.text: Left Brazil duty after its World Cup round-of-sixteen exit.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Santos contract renewal
strings.timeline.t2.text: The club announced an extension through the end of 2026.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Returns to Santos
strings.timeline.t3.text: Rejoined the club where he became famous after his Saudi spell.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joins Al-Hilal
strings.timeline.t4.text: Moved from Paris to Saudi Arabia; a severe knee injury later limited appearances.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Record Paris transfer
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined Paris Saint-Germain for €222 million, a record fee at the time.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Rio Olympic gold
strings.timeline.t6.text: Helped Brazil beat Germany in the final for its first men's Olympic title.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Barcelona treble
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won the domestic double and Champions League, sharing the European scoring lead.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Barcelona
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from Santos to Europe to play alongside Messi and others.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Copa Libertadores title
strings.timeline.t9.text: Helped Santos win South America's leading club competition.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Professional debut
strings.timeline.t10.text: Appeared for Santos's senior side and began his professional career.
